result.title: The Rhythm of Generated Video: Latent Chunking Leaves Periodic Traces in Compressed Bitstreams
result.comment: Manuscript, 9 pages, Computer vision, AI-generated video detection, compressed-domain analysis, video coding,
result.summary: Most AI-generated video detectors analyze decoded pixels and overlook how videos are produced. We show that causal video autoencoders leave an architecture-specific rhythm in compressed bitstreams: their temporal stride concentrates unpredictable content at latent-chunk boundaries, so rate-distortion optimized encoders allocate bits periodically. Without decoding pixels, we observe four-frame pulses in CogVideoX and Wan2.2 and eight-frame pulses in LTX-Video, which are absent from content-matched camera footage. Passing camera footage through a generator's autoencoder alone induces the pulse, supporting its proposed origin. A training-free peak-ratio statistic separates generated from camera video (AUC 0.84-0.94) and persists across tested quantization settings and H.264/H.265 encoding. Frame-size traces also identify four commercial generators, with 89.2%, 84.1%, and 83.0% accuracy under H.264, H.265, and AV1, beating the pixel-based UnivFD baseline (72.7-73.6%). Our results directly link generative architecture to measurable coding demand.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出因果视频自编码器的时间步幅使高不确定内容集中于 latent chunk 边界，导致压缩码流出现周期性比特分配脉冲（CogVideoX/Wan2.2 为四帧、LTX-Video 为八帧），并据此构建免训练的生成视频检测与生成器识别统计量。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 VLM 推理主线较远，但其「latent 分段边界承载不成比例的信息量且可从外部信号测出」的观察，可能为核查 latent 状态的分段粒度、边界位置对信息与计算分配的影响提供线索。
